# Synthetic AVIF interchange fixtures

These images contain generated mathematical patterns, with no external photo
assets. Ordinary Rust tests decode these files without native libraries. File
and generator SHA-256 hashes are recorded in `provenance.json`.

`p3-12bit` and `p3-10bit-crop-r1-m1` were generated by
`tools/validation/avif_precision.c`, using libavif 1.3.0 and AOM lossless encoding.
The RGBA16 expected samples come directly from the generator formula, including
alpha, crop, rotation, mirroring and full-range normalization. The cropped image
contains unequal Exif densities, which must swap with its quarter turn.

The three `hdr-*` files were generated by `tools/validation/avif_gainmap.c`, using
libavif 1.4.2 and AOM lossless encoding. Their base images are 12-bit Display P3
with straight alpha. Their 10-bit gain maps exercise per-channel gamma and
offsets, reduced monochrome samples, and BT.2020 application primaries distinct
from the base. The native libavif/dav1d decoder reopens each encoded container;
libavif's gain-map utility produces the `.rgba16f` references in linear sRGB.
That delivery utility clips negative RGB; the editing source retains it, so the
comparison clips only its reference comparison values to zero.

To regenerate the gain-map fixtures, build the validation-only C program with
the matching libavif 1.4.2 headers and library, then pass an output directory:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror tools/validation/avif_gainmap.c \
  $(pkg-config --cflags --libs libavif) -o /tmp/avif-gainmap-reference
/tmp/avif-gainmap-reference /tmp/avif-fixtures
```

The library must have AOM encoding and dav1d decoding enabled. Native codec
builds remain confined to independent fixture generation and comparison.
